newsitem.title: USA: Major stock movements overnight - June 3.
newsitem.headline: Major stock movements overnight - June 3.

text.p: NEW YORK - Wall Street stocks were weaker in late trade as blue chips failed to fully shake off an early decline. The long bond was unchanaged, yielding 6.91 percent. By 7.30 a.m. NZT the Dow Jones Index was off 31.33 points at 7,299.71.

LONDON - The UK's FTSE 100 index of leading shares chalked up its biggest one day decline in point terms for two months as bank stocks tumbled and fears grew of a possible rise in British interest rates later this week, worries over the Labour government's first budget, confirmed for July 2, also helped send the index 58.5 points lower at 4,562.8 -- its biggest fall since a 65-point loss on April 1.

FRANKFURT - German shares ended bourse trade strongly ahead, shrugging off earlier declines as market floundered on victory for the French left-wing in Sunday's poll and as the Bundesbank/Waigel row over assets revaluation continued apace. The 30-share DAX index ended at 3,605.62 up 57.78 points or 1.63 percent. In post-bourse trade the DAX index stood at 3,596.40.

PARIS - French shares ended higher, defying widespread expectations of a drastic fall after Sunday's Socialist election victory and the need for Communist support, one senior broker said the market recovery was "amazing" and the volume was huge, but much of the business was short-covering on trading positions
rather than buying by fund managers. The CAC-40 index closed up 17.71 points or 0.68 percent to 2,601.45.

ZURICH - Swiss shares bounced back from Friday's fall of nearly two percent in a technical reaction that pushed stocks up more than 100 points to close at the day's highs, short-covering, firming Swiss bonds and a rising U.S. dollar were seen as other major reasons for the advance. The broad Swiss Performance Index gained 63.27 points to 3,258.83.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks sprinted higher to end with gains of nearly two percent after finishing May on a negative note, buying interest in blue-chip issues and futures was especially strong throughout the day, although trade was thin. The Nikkei average added 383.04 points or 1.91 percent to close at 20,451.85.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks ended stronger with the blue-chip Hang Seng Index hitting another closing high on record turnover of HK$26.48 billion as liquidity continued to flow into the market. The Hang Seng index rose 233.09 points or 1.58 percent to finish at 14,990.90.

SYDNEY - Australian stocks bounded away in the afternoon to lock in another record close with the available investor interest clearly favouring the buy side. The All Ordinaries Index added 15.2 points to 2,625.7.

JOHANNESBURG - Robust gains in heavyweight industrial stocks, fomented by futures-basket trading, led South African shares up to the close as the market ignored the impact of a nationwide strike by the country's biggest union, stock gains were also in response to a hefty slide in industrials on Friday on expectations of a weak Wall Street, which went on to end flat. The industrial index finished up 50.2 points to 8,290.4,

Gold shares had another lacklustre day as bullion dipped below $344, pushing the index to yet another fresh four year closing low at 1,166.6 a fall of 7.6 points and the Overall index ended up 39.6 points at 7,061.3.
